name: Joshua/Joshua (High Priest)
title: The High Priest Who Restored Temple Service
summary: Joshua, son of Jozadak, was the high priest who led the rebuilding of the temple in Jerusalem after the exile in Babylon. He worked alongside Zerubbabel as the spiritual leader for the returned people. The prophet Zechariah used him as a messianic foreshadowing of the coming 'Branch'.

keyEvents.title: Rebuilding the Altar
keyEvents.description: Joshua and Zerubbabel rebuilt the altar and resumed offerings to the God of Israel shortly after returning from Babylon.

keyEvents.title: Laying the Temple Foundation
keyEvents.description: Under Joshua's spiritual leadership, the foundation of the second temple was laid, bringing great rejoicing and weeping among the people.

keyEvents.title: Opposing Resistance to Temple Construction
keyEvents.description: Jeshua and Zerubbabel rejected the offer from the enemies of the people to participate in temple construction, which led to delays.

keyEvents.title: Haggai's Encouragement
keyEvents.description: The prophet Haggai encouraged Jeshua and Zerubbabel to complete the temple construction with a promise of God's blessing and presence.

keyEvents.title: Zechariah's Vision of the Filthy Garments
keyEvents.description: Zechariah received a vision in which Jeshua stood before the angel of the Lord in filthy clothes that were exchanged for festive garments, symbolizing God's forgiveness.

keyEvents.title: The Coronation as a Messianic Foreshadowing
keyEvents.description: Zechariah was commanded to make crowns and place them on Jeshua's head as a prophetic sign of the coming Messiah, called 'Branch'.
